name: Question 12
problem:
Let $R=[0,4]\times [0,2]$ be a region in the $xy$-plane, and let $f(x,y)$ be a function defined over $R.$
The lower and upper Riemann sums corresponding to an arbitrary partition $P$ of $R$ are given by

$$
\begin{aligned}L(f,P) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}(4{x}_{i-1}+2{y}_{j-1})Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}, \\ U(f,P) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}(4{x}_{i}+2{y}_{j})Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the definition of the double integral in terms of $L(f,P)$ and $U(f,P),$ compute ${∬}_{R}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A.$

*Hint: You may wish to make use of the following result:*

$$
{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}({x}_{i-1}+{x}_{i})Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}=({x}_{m}^{2}-{x}_{0}^{2})({y}_{n}-{y}_{0})
$$
worked_solution:
For a function $f(x,y),$ the double integral of $f$ over a rectangular region $R$ is the unique number $I$ (if it exists) such that

$$
L(f,P)\le I\le U(f,P)
$$

over all partitions $P$ of $R.$

First, notice that ${\overset{¯}{x}}_{i}=\frac{1}{2}({x}_{i-1}+{x}_{i})$ will always lie between ${x}_{i-1}$ and ${x}_{i}$, and similarly ${\overset{¯}{y}}_{j}=\frac{1}{2}({y}_{j-1}+{y}_{j})$ will always lie between ${y}_{j-1}$ and ${y}_{j}.$ Therefore,

$$
4\cdot {x}_{i-1}+2\cdot {y}_{j-1}\le 4\cdot \frac{1}{2}({x}_{i-1}+{x}_{i})+2\cdot \frac{1}{2}({y}_{j-1}+{y}_{j})\le 4\cdot {x}_{i}+2\cdot {y}_{j}
$$

which simplifies to 

$$
4{x}_{i-1}+2{y}_{j-1}\le 2({x}_{i-1}+{x}_{i})+({y}_{j-1}+{y}_{j})\le 4{x}_{i}+2{y}_{j}.
$$

Multiplying this by $Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}$ and applying the double summation gives:

$$
L(f,P)\le {\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}[2({x}_{i-1}+{x}_{i})+({y}_{j-1}+{y}_{j})]Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}\le U(f,P)
$$

Separating the sums using the addition and constant multiple rules, we get

$$
L(f,P)\le 2{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}({x}_{i-1}+{x}_{i})Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}+{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}({y}_{j-1}+{y}_{j})Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}\le U(f,P).
$$

Using the hint, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}2{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}({x}_{i-1}+{x}_{i})Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j} & =2({4}^{2}-{0}^{2})(2-0)=64 \\ {\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}({y}_{j-1}+{y}_{j})Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j} & =({2}^{2}-{0}^{2})(4-0)=16\end{aligned}
$$

Finally then:

$$
\begin{aligned}L(f,P)\le 64+16\le U(f,P)\,⟹\,L(f,P)\le 80\le U(f,P)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that 

$$
{∬}_{R}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A=80.
$$

Let R=[0,4]×[0,2] be a region in the xy-plane, and let f(x,y) be a function defined over R. The lower and upper Riemann sums corresponding to an arbitrary partition P of R are given by

L(f,P)=∑i=1m∑j=1n(4xi−1+2yj−1)ΔxiΔyj,U(f,P)=∑i=1m∑j=1n(4xi+2yj)ΔxiΔyj.

Using the definition of the double integral in terms of L(f,P) and U(f,P), compute ∬Rf(x,y)dA.

Hint: You may wish to make use of the following result: ∑i=1m∑j=1n(xi−1+xi)ΔxiΔyj=(xm2−x02)(yn−y0)

EXPLANATION

For a function f(x,y), the double integral of f over a rectangular region R is the unique number I (if it exists) such that L(f,P)≤I≤U(f,P) over all partitions P of R.

First, notice that x¯i=12(xi−1+xi) will always lie between xi−1 and xi, and similarly y¯j=12(yj−1+yj) will always lie between yj−1 and yj. Therefore, 4⋅xi−1+2⋅yj−1≤4⋅12(xi−1+xi)+2⋅12(yj−1+yj)≤4⋅xi+2⋅yj which simplifies to 4xi−1+2yj−1≤2(xi−1+xi)+(yj−1+yj)≤4xi+2yj.

Multiplying this by ΔxiΔyj and applying the double summation gives: L(f,P)≤∑i=1m∑j=1n[2(xi−1+xi)+(yj−1+yj)]ΔxiΔyj≤U(f,P)

Separating the sums using the addition and constant multiple rules, we get L(f,P)≤2∑i=1m∑j=1n(xi−1+xi)ΔxiΔyj+∑i=1m∑j=1n(yj−1+yj)ΔxiΔyj≤U(f,P).

Using the hint, we get the following: 2∑i=1m∑j=1n(xi−1+xi)ΔxiΔyj=2(42−02)(2−0)=64∑i=1m∑j=1n(yj−1+yj)ΔxiΔyj=(22−02)(4−0)=16

Finally then: L(f,P)≤64+16≤U(f,P)⟹L(f,P)≤80≤U(f,P)

Therefore, we conclude that ∬Rf(x,y)dA=80.
